newsitem.title: CHINA: China to unveil firms set for foreign share offers.
newsitem.headline: China to unveil firms set for foreign share offers.

text.p: China will soon announce another group of companies that have been granted approval to list their shares abroad, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

The newspaper quoted Ma Zhongzhi, director of the State Council's Securities Commission, as saying that the companies included in what Beijing refers to as the fourth batch of such firms had been chosen after careful screening.
Ma was also quoted as saying overseas institutions were consulted in the screening process. He did not elaborate.
The chief of the securities policy making body of the State Council, or cabinet, made the remarks in a meeting with a Hong Kong business delegation on Monday.
Chinese officials have said they expected to announce this month the next group of companies cleared for foreign listings.
Most of the companies granted such approvsl in the past have listed their shares on the Hong Kong stock exchange.

A steep slide in shares on the domestic stock markets in Shanghai and southern China's Shenzhen have dragged down prices of H shares -- shares of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong -- this week.
The newspaper did not say what impact that would have on the timing or pricing of the next batch of public offerings.
